ai.definition: Cybersecurity for AI systems involves safeguarding artificial intelligence applications, platforms, and the underlying data against unauthorized access, breaches, and other cyber threats. This includes protecting both the hardware and software components of AI systems.
ai.howItWorks: This is achieved through a combination of security protocols such as encryption, authentication mechanisms, and regular vulnerability assessments. It also involves monitoring network traffic for anomalies and implementing intrusion detection systems to prevent unauthorized access or data exfiltration.
ai.problemSolved: The primary issue addressed by cybersecurity for AI systems is the protection against cyber threats that can compromise the integrity, availability, and confidentiality of AI applications and their associated data. This ensures that AI systems operate reliably and securely without being exploited by malicious actors.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing processes focus on creating secure hardware components that are resistant to physical tampering and software vulnerabilities. These include designing chips with built-in security features and ensuring the integrity of firmware updates.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves developing and testing security protocols, integrating them into AI systems, and conducting regular audits to ensure compliance with security standards. This includes creating secure boot processes, implementing secure communication channels, and ensuring that all software components are up-to-date with the latest security patches.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the development of advanced encryption methods, the implementation of robust authentication mechanisms, and continuous monitoring and updating of security protocols to address emerging threats. Additionally, there are costs associated with training personnel in cybersecurity best practices and maintaining compliance with relevant regulations.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook for cybersecurity in AI systems is positive as the reliance on AI technologies continues to grow across various industries. However, it remains a nascent market that requires ongoing investment in research and development to stay ahead of emerging threats.
ai.regulation: Regulations such as GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) mandate stringent data protection measures for organizations handling sensitive information. Compliance with these regulations drives the demand for robust cybersecurity practices within AI systems.
ai.risks: Risks include data breaches, unauthorized access to AI models, and potential manipulation of training datasets. These can lead to significant financial losses, reputational damage, and legal liabilities for organizations relying on AI technologies.
ai.profitability: Profitability is driven by the increasing reliance on AI across industries such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous vehicles. As more companies adopt AI solutions, there is a growing demand for cybersecurity services that can protect these systems from cyber threats.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development in this field will likely focus on enhancing encryption methods, developing machine learning-based threat detection systems, and integrating blockchain technology to ensure the integrity of AI data and models.

glossary.def: A software or hardware platform that uses artificial intelligence algorithms to perform tasks autonomously.
Any action, attempt, or risk of compromising the security of a digital system or network.
The protection of personal information from unauthorized access and disclosure.

subsystems.name: Supply-chain integrity
subsystems.role: ensures the data, weights and model files you run are the ones you intended to run.
parts: malware scanning of serialised model files
AI bill of materials listing components and dependencies

subsystems.name: Identity and access control
subsystems.role: decides which humans and services may train, deploy or query a model.

subsystems.name: Data protection and confidential computing
subsystems.role: keeps training data and prompts private, including from the infrastructure operator.
parts: encryption at rest and in transit
hardware trusted execution environments (for example Intel SGX, AMD SEV, NVIDIA confidential computing)

subsystems.name: Input and output guardrails
subsystems.role: stops hostile inputs and unsafe outputs at the model boundary.
parts: sandboxed tool calling with least privilege for agents

subsystems.name: Adversarial testing and monitoring
subsystems.role: finds and detects attacks that bypass the guardrails.

subsystems.name: Governance and response
subsystems.role: turns findings into fixes and manages incidents when prevention fails.

buildSteps.title: Inventory the AI assets
buildSteps.detail: List every model, dataset, endpoint, agent and third-party API in use, with an owner. You cannot defend what you have not catalogued.

buildSteps.title: Threat-model the pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Work through each stage — data collection, training, fine-tuning, deployment, inference, retirement — and name the attacks that apply: poisoning, evasion, prompt injection, model theft, supply-chain compromise, insider misuse.

buildSteps.title: Harden the supply chain
buildSteps.detail: Verify data sources, scan downloaded model files for embedded code, prefer safe serialisation formats over executable ones, pin dependency versions and sign the artefacts you release.

buildSteps.title: Lock down the infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: Segment the network, apply least-privilege identities, store secrets in a managed vault, encrypt data at rest and in transit, and run sensitive inference inside a trusted execution environment.

buildSteps.title: Build guardrails into the application
buildSteps.detail: Validate and sanitise inputs, screen prompts and outputs, restrict what tools an agent may call, cap query rates per user, and constrain what the model's responses can trigger downstream.

buildSteps.title: Instrument for detection
buildSteps.detail: Log prompts, tool calls and decisions with privacy controls, watch for extraction patterns, unusual query volumes and output drift, and plant canary data to catch leakage.

buildSteps.title: Test adversarially and continuously
buildSteps.detail: Run automated and human red teams, feed their attacks into regression suites, and gate model releases in CI/CD on security test results.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the response
buildSteps.detail: Write runbooks for model compromise, keep the ability to roll back or disable a model, rehearse disclosure and reporting, and fold lessons back into retraining and policy.

prerequisites.why: signing models, verifying artefacts and encrypting traffic all depend on mature key handling.
software bills of materials are established, but machine-learning-specific inventories of data and weights are still maturing.
attacks are well demonstrated; robust defences against evasion, poisoning and prompt injection remain unsolved in general.
confidential inference is available on some current server and accelerator hardware, but capacity, overhead and attestation coverage limit it.
tracking every transformation of a training set at scale is possible but rarely complete in practice.

pathway.milestone: model scanning, access control and guardrails applied to enterprise deployments
pathway.unlocks: a defensible baseline where the most common exposure paths are closed.

pathway.milestone: standardised AI bills of materials with signed weights and attestation
pathway.unlocks: buyers can verify what a model contains and where it came from.

pathway.milestone: automated red-teaming embedded in release pipelines
pathway.unlocks: continuous assurance as models are retrained and updated rather than one-off audits.

pathway.milestone: formal verification of narrow components and hard containment for autonomous agents
pathway.unlocks: limited provable guarantees, and the ability to let agents act with real permissions.

pathway.milestone: cross-border audit and disclosure norms for AI incidents
pathway.unlocks: shared evidence and faster coordinated response across organisations.
